gists: Farid, repay evil with good; do not let anger take hold of your heart.
Then no sickness will touch your body, and you will gain everything.
Farid, those who strike you with their fists, do not strike them back. Go to your own home, and kiss their feet.

gists: Mother, whom do I tell the pain of separation? My master’s love smoulders in me like a fire; stir it, and the embers glow red.
Sorrow is my bread, thorns are my curry, and my sighs are the firewood I burn.
Says humble faqir Hussain: if I meet my Beloved, I will bloom with joy.

posts.caption:
For someone who is far away. 🤍
Mian Muhammad Bakhsh

#MianMuhammadBakhsh #PunjabiPoetry #پنجابی_شاعری
posts.note: score-only reel; replaced by the lyric-reel format (2026-11-16)

gists: Hold the one point and drop the reckoning; clear away doubt and dread, and make the heart clean. It all comes down to one point.
You rub your forehead on the ground and show off a long prayer niche, yet the meaning never reaches your heart. Can truth stay hidden?
Many came home as pilgrims in fine blue robes, then sold their Hajj for coins. Who could admire that? Can truth stay hidden?
Some go off to the wilds and live on one grain a day, wearing out their bodies for nothing. Life runs out in such retreats.
Hold to the guide, be lost in carefree rapture, want nothing, and keep the heart clean. Bulleh, when was truth ever held back?

gists: You keep vigil all night and call yourself a shaikh; dogs keep vigil all night too. They are above you.
They never stop barking, then go and sleep on the rubbish heap. They are above you.
They never leave their master's door, though they are beaten a hundred times with shoes. They are above you.
Bulleh Shah, gather something for the journey, or the dogs will win the game. They are above you.

gists: It never sleeps, it only weeps: the body that carries the ache of pain is the one that weeps.
On the maiden's bed, no one has ever slept in comfort.
All four corners of my shawl are sunk in mud; who will wash them clean?
The cure for pain lives inside you; only a saintly healer can bring you to it.
Says Hussain, God's faqir: whatever is written is what comes to pass.

posts.title: اٹھ شاہ حسینا
posts.note: Owner asked for this kalam (2026-11-21, reference reel C25sn1Xosze, same 0–58 s of the track). Poet unidentified and not in our poem files: text read off the reference reel's screen and corrected against the audio (Whisper). Owner-approved exception to the files-only rule.

text:
اٹھ شاہ حسینا ویکھ لے
آسی بدلی بیٹھے بھیس

ساڈی جند نمانڑی کوکدی
آسی رُل گئے وچ پردیس

ساڈا ہر دم جی کرلاوندا
ساڈی نیر وگاوے اکھ

آساں جیوندی جان مر گئے
ساڈا مُد ہویا وکھ

سانوں سپ سویر دا ڈنگدا
سانوں پل پل چڑھدا زہر

ساڈے اندر بیلے شوق دے
جنگل بن گیا شہر

آساں سو غماں وچ ڈُبدے
ساڈی رُڑھ گئی نؤ پتوار

ساڈے بولنے تے پابندیاں
ساڈے سر لٹکے تلوار

آساں نیناں دے کھوہ گیڑ کے
کیتی وتر دل دی بھوں

اے بنجر رہی نمانڑیں
سانوں سجنڑاں تیری سوں
parts.source: on-screen text of instagram.com/reel/C25sn1Xosze, checked against Ramzan Jani's audio
gists: Rise, Shah Hussain, and see: we have changed our very guise.
Our poor soul cries out; we are lost, wandering in a strange land.
Every breath the heart wails, and the eyes keep shedding tears.
We died while still alive; we have been cut off from our own.
The snake of dawn bites us; its poison rises every moment.
Thickets of longing grow inside us; the city has become a jungle.
We drown in a hundred sorrows; our boat and oar have drifted away.
Our speech is in chains; a sword hangs over our heads.
We turned the wells of our eyes to water the soil of the heart.
Yet, poor thing, it stayed barren. Beloved, I swear by you.

gists: My Ranjha is someone else now.
The call rang out from the radiant throne, and it was heard in Lahore.
Those struck by love wander about, like cattle loose in the forest.
Ranjha, the lord of Takht Hazara, has slipped away from there like a thief.
Bulleh Shah, we are not the ones who die; it is someone else who lies in the grave.

gists: Love sets me swaying; my Beloved, grown close and bold, calls out to me.
Here a Shia, there a Sunni, here a matted-haired ascetic, there a silent sage; I stand apart from them all, and whatever I say, my Beloved accepts.
Bulleh came from far away, bewitched by His face; He showed that pure beauty, and I cannot forget it for a moment.
